identity.title: ALMA Observations of the Solar Chromosphere on the Polar Limb

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report the results of the Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) observations of the solar chromosphere on the southern polar limb.

evidence.quote: The target region was the solar south pole.

question.value: What dynamic structures (jets, blobs) does the solar polar-limb chromosphere show at 100 GHz in ALMA, and how do they correspond to IRIS and AIA features?

evidence.quote: By comparing with ultraviolet data obtained by the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS), we found a correspondence in the dynamic features in the ALMA data with IRIS spicules.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00201.S.
ALMA obtained Band-3 data in this time period within the 100 GHz frequency range.
The major and minor axes of the synthesized beam are 2.56$''$ (1.86 Mm on the Sun) in the east-west direction and 1.60$''$ (1.16 Mm) in the north-south direction, respectively.
The measured level of the noise is 13.2 K (Figure [4](#fig:noise)).
The observations were performed in $\approx$ 1 h around 14:30 UT on 2017 April 29.

provided.value: Si IV and Mg II slit-jaw images, 19 s cadence, 0.33-0.40'' resolution

evidence.quote: IRIS obtained slit-jaw images (SJIs) of Si IV and Mg II lines with a cadence and a spatial resolution of 19 s and $0.33$$''$­-$0.40$$''$ (240 – 290 km on the Sun), respectively.
provided context filtergrams of multiple wavelengths with a cadence of 12 s.

what.value: Solar disk brightness temperature of 7000 K used for absolute scale

evidence.quote: we assume that the brightness of the solar disk is 7000 K ((cite: avrett2008ApJS..175..229A)).

pipeline_or_manual.value: nominal solar-observation calibration of Shimojo et al. 2017b plus two-step phase self-calibration

evidence.quote: The ALMA data is calibrated with the nominal processes developed for solar observations in (cite: shimojo2017SoPh..292...87S).

self_calibration.value: two-step phase self-cal: model from whole-period image, then 20-s images as models per slot

evidence.quote: In the second step, we repeated the same procedure but synthesized images every 20 s and used each of them with a 20-s cadence as a calibration model for each data slot.
we synthesize each image with an integration time of 20 s

evidence.quote: The ALMA data is calibrated with the nominal processes developed for solar observations in (cite: shimojo2017SoPh..292...87S).

evidence.quote: the remaining signals can be regarded as noises ((cite: shimojo2017SoPh..292...87S)).

analysis_steps.goal: Relative brightness movie and comparison with IRIS/AIA

method.value: Relative brightness normalized by time-averaged Tb; compare limbs and jets with AIA 171 and IRIS Mg II

evidence.quote: is a temporally averaged brightness over the entire observed period ($\Delta t \approx 1 \ \mathrm{h}$).

method.value: Thermal free-free optical depth with Gaunt factor, tau ≈ Tb/T, EM≈n^2 L

evidence.quote: assuming a small optical thickness, 100% filling factor, and $L \approx 1.5\ensuremath{''}$ approximated with the width of the observed blob, and $\tau \approx T_b/T$
we obtain $n=(4.6-8.4) \times 10^{9}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ in the range of $T=(10^4- 4\times 10^5)\ \mathrm{K}$.

validation.value: Compared with spicule densities from IRIS spectra (Alissandrakis 2018): about an order of magnitude lower

evidence.quote: This number is a factor of one order of magnitude smaller than those for spicules obtained through the analysis of the IRIS spectrum data
The measured level of the noise is 13.2 K
The brightness enhancement in ALMA images is by 135 K beyond the background
The blob shows a systematic proper motion at a speed of 40 km/s
The speed of the elongation is 30–40 $\mathrm{km}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$.

findings_qualitative.value: ALMA 100 GHz limb shows saw-tooth patterns matching the AIA 171 limb; ALMA limb ~5'' above IRIS Mg II limb

evidence.quote: The IRIS Mg II limb (panel d) is $\approx$ 5$''$ below the ALMA limb.

claims.hypothesis: Do ALMA 100 GHz data show jet-like activity at the limb corresponding to IRIS spicules?
claims.experiment: Compare ALMA relative-brightness movie with IRIS Mg II SJIs
claims.result: Thorn-like structures ≥8'' long match IRIS jet clusters
claims.finding: ALMA detects jet-like activity associated with spicules

evidence.quote: These ALMA jets are in good correspondence with IRIS jet clusters.

claims.hypothesis: Can a blob ejection be traced and characterized?
claims.experiment: Track blob in ALMA and IRIS images; estimate density from free-free emission
claims.finding: Blob trajectory follows spicular patterns; density estimate likely biased by resolution/filling factor

evidence.quote: it is highly possible that $L$ is overestimated so that affecting the filling volume estimation in every dimension.

limitations_admitted.value: Absolute brightness temperature is hard to determine; S/N poor beyond 10'' off limb; resolution comparable to blob size

evidence.quote: it is still difficult to determine the absolute brightness temperature in the ALMA data

limitations_admitted.value: Could not confirm jet generation models

evidence.quote: Using the available data in the present observations, we could not confirm the proposed model.

referee_caveats_inferred: Self-calibration on 20 s models may bias structures
Density estimate depends on assumed T range and filling factor
No uncertainties on speeds or lengths

missing_for_reproduction: Measurement procedures for jets and blob

reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Recipe incomplete and results largely qualitative.
